title: LLM Inference Performance Optimization
overview: Systematically benchmark and optimize the Nemotron inference stack to reduce latency (<15s P50), increase throughput (>8 req/min), fit full AI pipeline on single RTX A5500 (24GB), and maintain quality (≥95% of 30B baseline). Uses benchmark-first approach - measure everything, decide with data.

phases.name: Phase 1: Benchmark Infrastructure
phases.objective: Build measurement foundation before any optimizations - latency, throughput, VRAM, and quality metrics

online: JSON schema validation for quality scoring
decisions: 100-event evaluation set (70 low, 20 medium, 8 high, 2 critical)
Four test scenarios: single request, sustained load, burst, cold start
Output as JSON reports with markdown comparison tool

create.purpose: Main benchmark runner orchestrating all test scenarios

unit: VRAM polling returns valid GPU memory stats
Quality scorer calculates risk score delta correctly
integration: Full benchmark run completes against live Nemotron service
Results JSON contains all required metrics

acceptance_criteria: Baseline captured for current 30B Q4_K_M llama.cpp setup
Comparison tool generates readable markdown tables

phases.name: Phase 2: Model Comparison
phases.objective: Benchmark Nemotron 30B/9B/8B/4B variants to determine if smaller models meet quality threshold

decisions: Quality threshold: 95% of 30B baseline to consider adoption
Test all models with same prompts, same parameters

create.purpose: Run benchmark suite across multiple models

unit: Model loader handles different GGUF files
Quality comparison calculates relative scores correctly
integration: Each model produces valid JSON responses
edge_cases: Model too large for available VRAM

acceptance_criteria: All 4 models benchmarked with same evaluation set
Model recommendation made based on 95% threshold

phases.name: Phase 3: Quantization Exploration
phases.objective: Test aggressive quantization formats (Q3_K, Q2_K, IQ variants) to find optimal VRAM/quality tradeoff

codebase: Need 3-5GB savings to fit full stack on A5500
online: IQ3_M offers better quality than Q3_K at similar size
IQ2_M offers better quality than Q2_K at similar size
llama.cpp supports all GGUF quantization formats
decisions: Test Q4_K_S, Q3_K_M, Q3_K_S, Q2_K, IQ3_M, IQ2_M
Compare 9B@Q4 vs 30B@Q3 if both meet quality threshold

unit: VRAM measurement accurate for each quantization
integration: Each quantization format loads and runs inference
Results capture VRAM savings vs quality loss

acceptance_criteria: Optimal quantization selected for winning model

phases.name: Phase 4: vLLM Engine Evaluation
phases.objective: Evaluate vLLM as inference backend for continuous batching and PagedAttention benefits

codebase: Existing Triton migration plan at docs/plans/triton-migration.md
online: vLLM provides PagedAttention for 2-4x memory efficiency
Prefix caching reduces latency for shared system prompts
decisions: Deploy vLLM alongside llama.cpp for A/B comparison
Test with winning model from Phase 2
If vLLM ≥5x throughput AND fits 24GB, migrate

unit: vLLM container starts and responds to health check
OpenAI-compatible API works with existing client
integration: Full benchmark suite runs against vLLM

acceptance_criteria: vLLM benchmarked against llama.cpp with same model
Engine recommendation made based on fit and performance

phases.name: Phase 5: Batching and Scheduling Optimization
phases.objective: Maximize throughput through priority queues, request coalescing, and PARALLEL tuning

codebase: Priority queue infrastructure exists but underutilized
online: Continuous batching can coalesce similar requests
Priority scheduling ensures critical alerts processed first
decisions: Priority levels: P0 (weapon/unknown night), P1 (unknown vehicle), P2 (normal), P3 (known faces)
Tune PARALLEL based on winning engine

create.purpose: Merge similar detections into single inference

modify.changes: Add priority scheduling and coalescing integration

integration: Burst of 10 detections processed with priority ordering

acceptance_criteria: Priority scheduling routes critical alerts faster
Request coalescing reduces inference count by 20-40%
Throughput gains measured under realistic load

phases.name: Phase 6: Integration and Validation
phases.objective: Combine winning optimizations and validate end-to-end against success criteria

decisions: Fallback: document optimal A5500+A400 split if single-GPU fails

modify.changes: Update deployment guide with new settings

integration: Full stack starts on A5500 without OOM

risks: Smaller models may not meet 95% quality threshold
vLLM may not fit winning model in 24GB
Aggressive quantization may hurt quality too much
Benchmarks may not reflect real-world workload patterns
